bug_semantics: A crafted CFB directory can make the child-directed binary-search path cycle through LeftSiblingId/RightSiblingId entries. DirectoryTree.TryGetDirectoryEntry repeatedly compares the requested name and follows one sibling while child is non-null; the pre-fix TryGetSibling check validates only the current parent/sibling ordering, so a multi-node cycle can satisfy every local comparison and never reach a match or NoStream. RootStorage.OpenStorage/TryOpenStorage/OpenStream/TryOpenStream all reach this lookup, leaving the affected thread in an uncatchable CPU-consuming loop.
flaw_origin: Commit 92cc9d74b7c4a63cf78625fbeaa5fa9207a01344 introduced OpenMcdf3/DirectoryTree.cs and, specifically, the new direct BST name-lookup implementation: while child is non-null it compares the target with child.NameCharSpan and replaces child with the selected LeftSiblingId or RightSiblingId entry, with no visited-node, step-bound, or whole-search-order state. This was not merely a path move: its direct parent used DirectoryTreeEnumerator.MoveTo for lookup and had no DirectoryTree.cs or child-directed BST lookup loop; 92cc9d74 newly wrote the mechanism fixed by the advisory patch.
ai_marker: absent: the exact commit object for 92cc9d74b7c4a63cf78625fbeaa5fa9207a01344 has author Jeremy Powell <jeremy@visionaid.com>, committer Jeremy Powell <jeremy@visionaid.com>, subject 'Add initial DirectoryTree implementation', and no message body or Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot, or other AI marker.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/openmcdf/openmcdf/security/advisories/GHSA-5qwm-7pvp-w988 identifies CVE-2026-45785/GHSA-5qwm-7pvp-w988, OpenMcdf/DirectoryTree.cs:35-46 and DirectoryEntries.cs:84-85, the OpenStorage/TryOpenStorage/OpenStream/TryOpenStream attack paths, affected versions <=3.1.3, and patched version 3.1.4. `git log -L 26,51:OpenMcdf/DirectoryTree.cs` traces the child-directed TryGetDirectoryEntry loop to 92cc9d74b7c4a63cf78625fbeaa5fa9207a01344; that commit's first-party page is https://github.com/openmcdf/openmcdf/commit/92cc9d74b7c4a63cf78625fbeaa5fa9207a01344 and its patch adds OpenMcdf3/DirectoryTree.cs lines 23-52 containing the unbounded loop. `git ls-tree -r --name-only cb9cb9d7cb0d5fa8e12577631f106dd810fb1966 -- OpenMcdf3/DirectoryTree.cs` returns no path, and direct inspection of cb9cb9d7cb0d5fa8e12577631f106dd810fb1966:OpenMcdf3/DirectoryTreeEnumerator.cs shows lookup instead went through MoveTo/MoveNext, proving the advisory's direct child-selected BST loop absent from the immediate parent. `git cat-file commit 92cc9d74b7c4a63cf78625fbeaa5fa9207a01344` proves the one-parent commit object and the exact human author/committer/message with no AI trailer. The direct first-party fix https://github.com/openmcdf/openmcdf/commit/c6f82db722bd85db7b0caed3ca1aa374f1e07bc7 says 'Fixes: GHSA-5qwm-7pvp-w988'; it adds OpenMcdf/DirectoryTreeSearchOrderValidator.cs, carries min/max bounds across each search, and changes OpenMcdf/DirectoryTree.cs plus OpenMcdf/DirectoryEntries.cs so every selected sibling is checked against the accumulated global bounds, causing a cyclic path to throw FileFormatException instead of repeating. Its RootStorageTests.cs regression opens DirectoryTreeCycle.cfb and expects FileFormatException from TryOpenStorage. Boundary checks resolve v3.1.3 to fd0775c58134848a587424c4a9d6c2403f628e19 and v3.1.4 to 11ffb7cafff6eea99639df6b2b249dcf6bcca3ef; `git tag --contains 92cc9d74b7c4a63cf78625fbeaa5fa9207a01344` includes v3.0.0-preview.1 through v3.1.3, while `git tag --contains c6f82db722bd85db7b0caed3ca1aa374f1e07bc7` starts at v3.1.4 (and v3.2.0), not v3.1.3. `git diff v3.1.3 v3.1.4 -- OpenMcdf/DirectoryTree.cs OpenMcdf/DirectoryEntries.cs OpenMcdf/DirectoryTreeSearchOrderValidator.cs` shows the vulnerable boolean/local sibling check at the last affected tag and the accumulated search-order validator at the first patched tag.
reasoning: The advisory's failure is specifically the direct BST name lookup, not the separately enumerated tree: attacker-controlled sibling IDs can revisit entries while preserving each immediate left/right ordering relation, so the old local validation does not make the loop's child-null exit reachable. History establishes 92cc9d74b7c4a63cf78625fbeaa5fa9207a01344 as the smallest commit that first wrote this child-selected lookup loop in a newly added DirectoryTree.cs; its parent lacks both the file and that algorithm, while later renames and validation refactors preserve the loop and therefore are not BICs. The fix c6f82db722bd85db7b0caed3ca1aa374f1e07bc7 is causal and direct: stateful min/max validation makes revisiting a node violate the accumulated BST range and its regression covers crafted-cycle lookup. Tag ancestry matches the stated 3.1.3/3.1.4 boundary. Finally, attribution is based only on the BIC commit object, which is human-authored/committed and contains no AI marker, so the closed verdict is NOT_AI.
